verse: I baptize you with water for repentance, but he who will come after me is more powerful than me. I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the fire of the Holy Spirit. (Matt 3:11)
This is the one about whom I said, “After me comes a man, who is greater than me, because he was before me.” (Jn 1:30)
I myself did not know him. Yet it is for this reason that I come baptizing with water: so that he may be revealed to Israel. (Jn 1:31)
Jesus came from Galilee, to John at the Jordan, in order to be baptized by him. (Matt 3:13)
John tried to prevent him, saying, “I ought to be baptized by you, yet you have come to me.” (Matt 3:14)
Jesus answering, said to him, “Let it to be so for now. For in this way, we shall fulfill all righteousness.” Then John agreed. (Matt 3:15)
Jesus, having been baptized, ascended from the water immediately, and behold, the heavens were opened to him. And he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and alighting on him. (Matt 3:16)
Behold, there was a voice from heaven, saying: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” (Matt 3:17)
John offered testimony, saying: “For I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove; and he remained upon him.” (Jn 1:32)

I did not know him. But he who sent me to baptize with water said to me: ‘He over whom you will see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him, this is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.’ (Jn 1:33)
On the third day, a wedding was held in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. Now Jesus was also invited to the wedding, with his disciples. (Jn 2:1-2)
And when the wine had given out, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.” (Jn 2:3)
Jesus said to her: “What is that to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet arrived.” (Jn 2:4)
His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.” (Jn 2:5)
Now in that place, there were six stone water jars, for the purification ritual of the Jews, each holding twenty or thirty gallons. (Jn 2:6)
Jesus said to them, “Fill the water jars with water.” And they filled them to the very top. (Jn 2:7)
Jesus said to them, “Now draw from it, and carry it to the chief steward of the feast.” And they took it to him. (Jn 2:8)
When the chief steward had tasted the water made into wine, since he did not know where it was from, for only the servants who had drawn the water knew, the chief steward called the groom. (Jn 2:9)
He said to him: “Everyone offers the good wine first, and then, when they have become drunk, they offer what is inferior. But you have kept the good wine until now.” (Jn 2:10)
This was the beginning of the signs that Jesus accomplished in Cana of Galilee, and it manifested his glory, and his disciples believed in him. (Jn 2:11)
The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Repent and believe in the Gospel. (Mrk 1:15)
Jesus answered, “Amen, amen, I say to you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.” (Jn 3:5)
From that time, Jesus began to preach, and to say: “Repent. For the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” (Matt 4:17)
Jesus traveled throughout all of Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the Gospel of the kingdom, and healing every sickness and every infirmity among the people. (Matt 4:23)
Going forth, preach, saying: ‘For the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.’ Cure the infirm, raise the dead, cleanse lepers, cast out demons. You have received freely, so give freely. (Matt 10:7-8)

Into whatever city you have entered and they have received you, eat what they set before you. And cure the sick who are in that place, and proclaim to them, ‘The kingdom of God has drawn near to you.’ (Luk 10:8-9)
This Good News about the Kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the world as a testimony to all the nations; and then the end will come. (Matt 24:14)
It happened afterwards that he was making a journey through the cities and towns, preaching and evangelizing the kingdom of God. And the twelve were with him. (Luk 8:1)
When the crowd had realized this, they followed him. And he received them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God. And those who were in need of cures, he healed. (Luk 9:11)
Jesus traveled throughout all of the cities and towns, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the Gospel of the kingdom, and healing every illness and every infirmity. (Matt 9:35)
After six days, Jesus took Peter and James and his brother John, and he led them onto a high mountain, by themselves. (Matt 17:1)
He was transfigured before them. And his face shined brightly like the sun. And his garments were made white like snow. (Matt 17:2)
Behold, there appeared to them Moses and Elijah, speaking with him. (Matt 17:3)
His clothes became dazzling white, such as no one on earth is able to bleach them. (Mrk 9:3)
Peter responded by saying to Jesus: “Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you are willing, let us make three dwellings here, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” (Matt 17:4)

While he was still speaking, behold, a shining cloud overshadowed them. And behold, there was a voice from the cloud, saying: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased. Listen to him.” (Matt 17:5)
The disciples, when they heard the voice, they fell on their faces and were very afraid. (Matt 17:6)
Jesus drew near and touched them. And he said to them, “Rise up and do not be afraid.” (Matt 17:7)
Lifting up their eyes, they saw no one, except Jesus alone. (Matt 17:8)
As they were descending from the mountain, Jesus instructed them, saying, “Tell no one about the vision, until the Son of man has risen from the dead.” (Matt 17:9)
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples approached Jesus, saying, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?” (Matt 26:17)
Jesus said, “Go into the city, to a certain man, and say to him: ‘The Teacher says: My time is near. I am observing the Passover with you, along with my disciples.’” (Matt 26:18)
The disciples did just as Jesus had directed them. And they prepared the Passover. (Matt 26:19)
When evening arrived, he sat at the table with his twelve disciples. And while they were eating, he said: “Amen I say to you, that one of you is about to betray me.” (Matt 26:20-21)
Being greatly saddened, each one of them began to say, “Surely, it is not I, Lord?” But he responded by saying: “The one who dips his hand into the bowl with me will betray me.” (Matt 26:22-23)
Indeed, the Son of man goes, just as it has been written about him. But woe to that man by whom the Son of man will be betrayed. It would be better for that man if he had not been born. (Matt 26:24)
While they were eating the meal, Jesus took bread, and he blessed and broke and gave it to his disciples, and he said: “Take and eat. This is my body.” (Matt 26:26)
Taking the chalice, he gave thanks. And he gave it to them, saying: “Drink from this, all of you.” (Matt 26:27)
This is my blood of the new covenant, which shall be shed for many for the forgiveness of sins. (Matt 26:28)
But I say to you, I will not drink again from this fruit of the vine, until that day when I will drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father. (Matt 26:29)
